title: Comments in Go
learning_outcomes: Explain the purpose and behavior of comments in go.
Apply at least one lesson concept—single-line comments—in a small Go example or workflow.
Predict a representative result, then test a boundary case and explain any difference.

content.intro: Comments in Go gives you a rule for reading or writing Go programs. Go is statically typed and its syntax is intentionally regular; read the declarations and expressions from their types and scope, then predict what each statement changes. The Go specification is the authoritative reference for exact behavior.
content.why_it_matters: Small language rules have a large effect: they determine whether a program compiles and whether edge cases behave as expected.

content.task: Create a small example connected to “Comments in Go”. Use Single-line comments as the starting point, predict the output, then add one invalid, empty, or boundary case and document its result.
task_acceptance_criteria: The example demonstrates single-line comments or a closely related concept.
Inputs, relevant state changes, and expected output are clear.
At least one boundary case is deliberately tested or documented.
Errors are handled honestly and no success state is reported when the operation fails.
hints: Start from the simplest example related to single-line comments.
Predict the result manually and annotate the value that changes at each step.
Run `gofmt` and the appropriate local `go run`, `go test`, `go vet`, or inspection command when prerequisites are available.

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming the happy-path output proves all inputs are safe.
common_mistakes.why: Empty, malformed, boundary, or concurrent cases may follow different paths.
common_mistakes.fix: Add focused tests for a normal input and at least one relevant edge case.

common_mistakes.problem: Ignoring returned errors or external-system status.
common_mistakes.why: Go APIs commonly report expected failures as explicit error values.
common_mistakes.fix: Check errors close to the operation, add useful context when propagating, and clean up resources.

common_mistakes.problem: Using an API or syntax without checking the selected Go version.
common_mistakes.why: Language and standard-library capabilities can change between releases.
common_mistakes.fix: Record `go version`, inspect the `go` directive, and read official release notes for version-specific topics.

summary: Comments in Go provides a reusable rule or workflow for Go programs.
The subtopics to revisit are: Single-line comments; Multiline comments; Documentation comments; Commenting exported declarations; Writing useful technical comments.
Prefer a small reproducible example, explicit errors, appropriate tests, and version-matched official documentation.
